lead: Yo — I'm Chad Underwood. I build useful software, write when something sticks, and keep a small corner of the internet that feels like leaving the rest of it. I care about craft, clarity, and the kind of work that ages well. Based somewhere between Nashville and the next idea. Always tinkering. Rarely boring.

words.title: Useful software
words.body: Tools that disappear into the day — Raycast-ish sharpness, Drafts-style capture, quiet automation. I ship products and side projects that remove friction rather than add dashboards.

words.title: Writing
words.body: Essays land here first. Drafts on the phone → publish → this site. No newsletter modal theater. Just words when there's something worth saying.

words.title: This site
words.body: Inspired by ped.ro's conversational bio and Benji Taylor's line about leaving the rest of the internet. Dark, calm, dock at the bottom. Built with Astro, hosted as static HTML.

words.title: Craft
words.body: Details that compound: typography, timing, the difference between a button that works and one that feels inevitable. Obsessive in the quiet places.

words.title: Clarity
words.body: Say the thing. Cut the hedges. Prefer one sharp sentence over three soft ones. Same for interfaces.

words.title: Work that ages well
words.body: Fewer trends, more foundations. Prefer boring technology when it wins. Prefer bold bets when the upside is asymmetric.

words.title: Nashville
words.body: Home base energy — music, humidity, and enough distance from the coasts to think clearly. Exact pin TBD; the vibe isn't.

words.title: The next idea
words.body: Usually arrives mid-walk or mid-shower. Captured in Drafts before it evaporates. Some become products. Some become essays. A few become secrets.

words.title: Always tinkering
words.body: Side projects, photo walks, dock icons at 2am. The site itself is a tinkering surface — hotspots, badges, time-of-day light shifts.

words.title: Rarely boring
words.body: Not chaos-for-chaos. Just a bias toward interesting problems, good people, and nights that end with something made.

words.title: Leaving the rest of the internet
words.body: Benji Taylor's idea: a personal site should feel like you've briefly left the feed. No engagement bait. No cookie walls. Just a room.

words.title: You found it
words.body: Quiet doors for quiet visitors. There's a page that isn't in the sitemap.
